entries.reason: Experiment 3 (salience priors), the derivation of idealised predictions (S1), type definitions (S2), experiment links (S3) and Bayes factor computation (S5) are in supplements that are not part of paper.pdf.
entries.impact: Experiment 3 is not modelled as a study; exact printed instructions, stimulus images and the salience priors needed for the R2 listener rule cannot be reproduced from the paper alone.
entries.suggested_action: Supply S1-S5 Text or the experiment materials in sources/ to extend the program.

entries.reason: The paper gives no age, gender or the number who completed versus started.
entries.impact: AI participants cannot be matched to the human sample demographically; no persona is simulated.
entries.suggested_action: Treat participants as unconditioned AI participants or supply demographics.

entries.reason: Only the recruited (60) and analysed counts are reported.
entries.impact: Randomised, retained and analysed sizes cannot be fully distinguished.
entries.suggested_action: Supply the completion count.

entries.reason: The paper does not state blinding.
entries.impact: No effect on the replay; participants are AI.
entries.suggested_action: None needed unless the researcher wants a statement.

entries.reason: The paper paraphrases what participants were told but prints no instruction text, screen or picture.
entries.impact: The replay prompts use a paraphrase of the reported instructions and text descriptions of objects and messages; this is a replay adaptation, not the original material.
entries.suggested_action: Supply the original instruction text and stimulus pictures in sources/ to make them verbatim.

entries.reason: The original stimuli are pictures (Fig 1) which text-only AI participants cannot see.
entries.impact: Objects and messages are rendered as text such as 'a green monster with a red hat'.
entries.suggested_action: Accept the text rendering or provide image-capable participants.

entries.reason: The 18 baseline fillers are described only as unambiguous or ambiguous; the split between the two kinds, the number of distinct displays and scoring details are not stated.
entries.impact: The replay chooses an even split (9 and 9) and the construction rules documented in task/task.json.
entries.suggested_action: Supply the split and the filler construction or confirm the assumption.

entries.reason: The paper does not say whether participants received feedback on their choices.
entries.impact: The replay gives no feedback; if feedback existed, learning might differ.
entries.suggested_action: Confirm that no feedback was given.

entries.reason: It is not stated whether the messages (comprehension) or the addressee (production) were real participants or scripted.
entries.impact: In the replay the message is the generated trigger message (a scripted stimulus) and no real addressee exists; this follows the stimulus description and is the only runnable reading.
entries.suggested_action: Confirm that messages were generated from the design, not taken from earlier participants.

entries.reason: The contrast weights are not printed, so coefficients are only comparable with the paper up to the coding.
entries.impact: The evaluator uses standard Helmert weights and fixed-effects logistic regression and flags the difference to the paper's mixed-effects model.
entries.suggested_action: Confirm weights or run glmer externally.
